questions.question: During a slow, tight turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with the motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans. This helps you maintain control.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either the front or rear brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice when the vehicle in front stops and to brake safely.

questions.question: Who sets the pace for a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace. This ensures no one gets left behind.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A passenger should get on only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as close to the front as you can without blocking the rider's control. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader at the front of the group. More experienced riders behind them can watch out for them.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which is NOT required?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader so experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A rider can use hand signals instead of turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should be over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can make the motorcycle harder to control.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who move into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to properly yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to move more slowly than they really do. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides with you, you should instruct them to do all of the following except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit as close as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist. Keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you wish to turn.
Avoid dragging your feet on the road.

questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Don't drag your feet on the road or you could lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: If you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle or have a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is on the right side, so riding too far right may cause it to go off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel could leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: When your motorcycle is stopped, which gear should you stay in?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while slowly increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be more visible. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. A staggered formation is used at other times.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing on the left. This gives you a better view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Maintain a minimum of two seconds behind the vehicle ahead. Use at least three seconds in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you from behind?

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a turn?

options.text: Move your shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a turn by closing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. Pick a position that gives you the most space and makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be true about a helmet?

options.text: It was worn in a previous accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It was worn in a previous accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no defects. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They will definitely yield to you.
They may not actually see you.
It is not worth the effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not actually see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver sees you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to notice them.
